channel.title: Michael Rooney — Journal
channel.description: Homelabbing, certifications, front-end development, and the process of transitioning into tech — documented as it happens.

item.title: The Fleet Got Slower Overnight, and Nothing Was Wrong
item.description: Chasing a real, alarming-looking performance regression across an entire homelab fleet down to its actual, benign cause — one layer of verification at a time.

item.title: Session 27 — Proving the Smoke Test Actually Smokes
item.description: A post-deploy smoke test confirmed both directions against real infrastructure — a real passing deploy, and a real killed proxy proving it genuinely fails loudly, not just looks correct.

item.title: Session 26 — Three Bugs, a Disk, and an Idempotency Check That Actually Worked
item.description: Idempotency verification built and run for real against all three flagged playbooks — surfacing a corrupted fstab UUID that had quietly filled a root filesystem to 100%, among three other real bugs.

item.title: Smoke Test Doesn't Mean What the Exit Code Thinks It Means
item.description: A deploy command returning success only proves the command ran — a smoke test is the difference between that and actually asking the deployed thing if it's working.

item.title: Session 25 — Closing Phase 2: A Database, a Decision, and a Comparison, All Made Testable
item.description: Phase 2 of automated test coverage closed for real — db.ts tested against a real in-memory database, and two pure decision functions extracted specifically to make untestable logic testable.

item.title: Session 24 — Two Columns, and the Breakpoint That Was Wrong the First Time
item.description: Incident history moved into its own column, separate from category status — and a real breakpoint mistake caught by actually looking at the result, not just the code.

item.title: Session 23 — The Badge, the Fixture, and the Gap We Finally Closed
item.description: The embeddable status badge, built and confirmed live — then a real fixture-based parity test closing a gap flagged since 18- was first scoped, confirmed green in CI.

item.title: Optimizing for an Audience That Doesn't Click
item.description: What SEO actually optimizes for, why AEO is a different target rather than a rebrand of the same thing, and applying both to a small personal portfolio with Person and BlogPosting schema.

item.title: Session 22 — GitHub Actions, and a Folder That Never Existed
item.description: Building real CI for both repos surfaced a structural mismatch every scope doc had wrong, a deliberate vault-secret tradeoff, and a permanently-failing check fixed properly.

item.title: A Fixture Is Just Test Data With a Job
item.description: What a fixture is, why it's different from just 'more tests,' and the real bug it's designed to prevent — a value mismatch nobody catches until production.

item.title: Session 21 — Security Hardening, and the Proxy That Trusted Everyone
item.description: A secrets audit that found something bigger than a leaked credential — three unrestricted authenticated proxies — fixed with real allowlists, confirmed live.

item.title: CI and CD Are Not One Thing
item.description: Why 'CI/CD' is really two separate decisions, and the real reason one half is easy and the other isn't, for a homelab behind an outbound-only tunnel.

item.title: Publishing Isn't the Same as Protecting
item.description: What a Cloudflare Tunnel actually is, and a real gotcha: publishing a route makes it public by default — protecting it is a separate step.

item.title: Session 20 — Manual Incident Authoring, and Two Routing Bugs Nginx Was Hiding
item.description: The last big workflow gap, closed — with a real dedup bug caught before shipping, Cloudflare Access with zero application code, and two genuine nginx routing bugs found in production.

item.title: Duplication Isn't the Enemy — Silent Drift Is
item.description: Why the obvious fix for duplicated code isn't always the right one, and why a concrete trigger beats 'keep an eye on it' for revisiting an architecture decision.

item.title: A Promise You Can Check Automatically
item.description: What a test file actually does, what pass/fail means (and doesn't), whether every file deserves a test, and why a small new lib/ folder was the right call.

item.title: Session 19 — The First Real Tests, and a Folder Nobody Planned For
item.description: 23 tests targeting real documented bug history, a react-refresh lint catch, a new lib/ directory, and a scope doc for testing the deployment playbooks next.

item.title: The Difference Between Asking and Being Told
item.description: What SSE actually is, why a signal-only nudge channel can be worth more than the data it doesn't carry, and a real Cloudflare bug found in testing.

item.title: Session 18 — A Nudge Channel, and the Silence Cloudflare Wouldn't Tolerate
item.description: The hybrid SSE nudge channel, a real Cloudflare idle-timeout bug found in testing, and both directions confirmed live against production.

item.title: Session 17 — Auto-Drafted Incidents, and the Build Assumption That Wasted Twenty Minutes
item.description: A new drafted-incidents table, threshold detection re-derived from real data, a live production test end to end, and a stale build assumption that cost real time.

item.title: One Hex Code, Two Different Verdicts
item.description: What WCAG contrast ratios actually measure, and why the same color can pass against one background and fail against another — with a real example.

item.title: Session 16 — A Full Restyle, and the One Color That Didn't Pass
item.description: A component-by-component token replacement, real portfolio typography, and a WCAG contrast failure caught in the accent color and fixed at the source.

item.title: The Shortcut Everyone Already Knows How to Use
item.description: Building a Cmd+K command palette from scratch — the guarded keydown listener, keyboard nav, focus management, and a state-sync bug you'll probably hit too.

item.title: Session 15 — A Command Palette, and the Same Bug Caught Twice
item.description: A hand-rolled Cmd+K command palette, reusing the existing detail view and adding a new category filter — plus a lint rule that caught the same state-sync mistake in two different components.

item.title: Session 14 — Click Into a Node, See What It's Actually Doing
item.description: Response-time tracking and a per-service detail view, built together — a hand-rolled line chart, a real Prometheus job-name bug, and confirming both data paths independently.

item.title: The Half-Second Nobody's Supposed to See
item.description: How a theme toggle avoids a flash of the wrong theme on load, and how Tailwind v4's CSS-native @theme system makes it possible without touching every component.

item.title: Session 13 — A Toggle, and Three Contrast Bugs It Was Right to Catch
item.description: Building the color-token system and light/dark toggle — Tailwind v4's @theme directive, an anti-flash script, and real contrast bugs a manual test caught.

item.title: Session 12 — Four Small Things, One Real Lint Chain
item.description: A dynamic tab title and favicon, skeleton loading states, a days-since-last-incident counter, documented public API routes, and a genuine three-layer ESLint purity chase.

item.title: Three Small Lies a Working Ansible Collection Told Me
item.description: Scripting Zabbix host registration with community.zabbix — a changed auth model, a become setting that breaks over an API connection, and a template permission scope that isn't the host permission scope.

item.title: What a Scraper Actually Is, and How Mine Works
item.description: What a scraper actually is, the pieces every one needs, what they're used for, and a walkthrough of a real one already built and shipped in my homelab status page.

item.title: Session 11 — Giving Every Category Real History
item.description: Scoping and building full-category uptime history for Proxmox API and Zabbix — a proxy-side snapshot poller, a dead-code bug found along the way, and a checklist applied before deploying instead of after.

item.title: Scope Isn't Overhead — It's the Actual Work
item.description: What 'scope' actually means, why it matters more than the build itself, and a repeatable process for scoping a project or feature yourself.

item.title: Session 10 — Incident History, and Five Bugs on the Way There
item.description: Building incident history end to end, and the trail of real bugs it took to get there — tooling, timezones, filenames, and a missing nginx route.

item.title: Chasing a Blue Line That Wasn't There
item.description: A pass through the site's mobile experience — full-card project links that surfaced a real hidden-link bug, a nav hamburger rolled out across all 33 pages, a missing data-label attribute, and a debugging detour into a blue underline that turned out to be a stale phone cache.

item.title: Google IT Support, Done — Network+, Still Waiting
item.description: Finishing the Google IT Support certificate on top of a 45+ hour work week, the capstone build, and capstone-adjacent research — and being honest about why the Network+ exam itself is still just sitting there unscheduled.

item.title: Session 9 — Real History, and Two Loose Ends Tied Off
item.description: Wiring the 90-day uptime bars to real Prometheus data, fixing a cloudflared idempotency gap, rewriting the Ansible reference doc, and tracing a fleet-wide monitoring gap to a physical rack rebuild.

item.title: Session 8 — Deployment Day: Dockerfiles, a Single Origin, and a Password That Got Away
item.description: Taking the capstone status page live — the missing Dockerfiles, a single-origin nginx reverse proxy, a crash-looping proxy container, a leaked password, and a silently missing Prometheus category caught only after going public.

item.title: Session 7 — A VM, a VLAN, and a Backwards Firewall Rule
item.description: Provisioning the capstone Docker VM on Dega — a cloud-init build instead of the netinst installer, a VLAN double-tagging bug that broke Layer 2 entirely, three cloudflared token mistakes, and an OPNsense firewall rule that had source and destination reversed.

item.title: Giving the Capstone a Real Home
item.description: Standing up Dega as an isolated VLAN 20 node built specifically to host the capstone status page — retargeted Ansible playbooks, scoped firewall pinholes for the proxy's outbound calls, and the VM-vs-LXC decision that came from taking the isolation seriously.

item.title: The Math of a Shutdown Daemon
item.description: Deploying a secure Docker host on VLAN 20 for the capstone project uncovered a configuration conflict inside the NUT automation templates, proving that what looks fine static can easily break on boot.

item.title: Teaching the Lab to Talk Trash
item.description: A pure-fun side project — a small Flask relay that adds snark to Grafana alerts and Proxmox/PBS notifications before forwarding them to Discord, plus an SSH lockout on a freshly provisioned LXC and a first look at Proxmox's Handlebars webhook templating.

item.title: Two Hours to Spare
item.description: A wildcard cert renewal that failed silently until the real Certbot log revealed the actual cause — a Proxmox-level DNS misconfiguration pointing an LXC at Tailscale's resolver instead of the LAN, unrelated to the Cloudflare token I spent an hour chasing first.

item.title: Zabbix Online, Switch Offline
item.description: Completing Zabbix monitoring for all five Proxmox nodes — 606 items collecting — and discovering the Netgear GS308Ev4 doesn't support SNMP.

item.title: Session 6 — Zabbix Adapter and Four Live Data Sources
item.description: Building the Zabbix client adapter, debugging a Zabbix 7.x API change that moved agent availability into the interfaces object, and wiring the fourth data source into a fully operational status page.

item.title: Connection Reset by Peer
item.description: Deploying Zabbix Agent 2 across all five Proxmox nodes via Ansible — a version mismatch with the server, a 404 from a repo path that changed between Zabbix versions, and a missing log directory that crash-looped the service after the upgrade.

item.title: Session 5 — Zabbix, Debugging, and a Deliberate Deferral
item.description: Wiring up the Zabbix proxy route, debugging a wrong IP, fixing TypeScript strict mode errors, and making a deliberate decision to defer Zabbix configuration in favor of deployment momentum.

item.title: Session 4 — Proxmox Adapter and Debugging
item.description: Wiring up the Proxmox adapter, debugging NaN metrics, a missing Sys.Audit permission, and learning that the /nodes endpoint doesn't return what you think it does.

item.title: Session 3 — The Proxy Layer
item.description: Building an Express proxy to keep Proxmox API credentials off the browser — what a backend-for-frontend is, why CORS exists, and how dotenv keeps secrets out of source code.

item.title: Session 2 — Hook, Components, and First Live Render
item.description: TanStack Query hook, four UI components, and the first live render — six services pulling real data from Prometheus and NUT, plus debugging a label key mismatch in the UPS adapter.

item.title: Session 1 — Scaffold, Dependencies, and Data Layer
item.description: Fresh repo, Vite + React + TypeScript scaffold, Tailwind v4, TanStack Query provider, and the complete typed data layer talking to Prometheus and NUT before any UI exists.

item.title: N10-009 Study Notes: Review & What's Next
item.description: A full review of the N10-009 exam domains, what to focus on in the final week, and what the path to CCNA looks like from here.

item.title: N10-009 Study Notes: Troubleshooting
item.description: A practical walkthrough of Network+ domain 5 — the troubleshooting methodology, tools, and common failure scenarios — anchored to real homelab debugging sessions.

item.title: N10-009 Study Notes: Security & Operations
item.description: A practical walkthrough of Network+ domains 3 and 4 — firewalls, VPNs, AAA, SNMP, monitoring, and high availability — anchored to a real homelab.

item.title: N10-009 Study Notes: Network Implementation
item.description: A practical walkthrough of Network+ domain 2 — Ethernet, switching, VLANs, STP, wireless, and virtualization networking — anchored to a real five-node homelab.

item.title: N10-009 Study Notes: Networking Concepts
item.description: A practical walkthrough of Network+ domain 1 — the OSI model, IP addressing, subnetting, routing, and DNS — anchored to a real five-node homelab.

item.title: Going Dark for a Bit
item.description: The Network+ voucher is purchased. The exam is soon. Here's where the homelab stands, what I'm studying, and why CCNA is next.

item.title: Overdue Housekeeping
item.description: Splitting the project list into a dedicated portfolio showcase, wiring up new coursework projects, stripping the sitemap back to basics, and consolidating a scattered local repo structure.

item.title: One Place for Secrets
item.description: Deploying Vaultwarden as a self-hosted password manager — working through a Node 0 networking dead end, landing on Murloc, and using the existing Tailscale exit node for resilient access.

item.title: Two More Eyes
item.description: Deploying Zabbix for infrastructure state monitoring and Homelable for interactive topology visualization — plus the PostgreSQL loopback issue that took longer to find than it should have.

item.title: Automation Infrastructure
item.description: Standing up Ansible as a permanent part of the homelab — control node, inventory, vault, and the first playbooks enforcing consistent state across all five nodes.

item.title: Configuration as Code
item.description: Standing up an Ansible LXC, writing the first real playbooks, and using the process to audit NUT configs that turned out to have enough inconsistencies to warrant a full standardization pass.

item.title: Proactive Alerts
item.description: Moving beyond passive dashboards to a proactive alerting system for Proxmox and UPS infrastructure.

item.title: Metrics, Finally
item.description: Standing up Prometheus and Grafana across the homelab, debugging a peaNUT UPS integration that turned out to be running on dummy data, and learning why USB HID devices and LXC containers don't get along.

item.title: The Call
item.description: The networking conversation I'd been building toward for months finally happened. What I learned, what it means, and where it points next.

item.title: Restructuring the Infrastructure
item.description: Moving the backup server to dedicated bare metal, replacing a cluster node, adding UPS monitoring and temperature visibility — a significant infrastructure milestone.

item.title: Never Locked Out Again
item.description: After getting locked out of a Proxmox node tonight, I fixed the structural problem — migrating the Tailscale exit node out of OPNsense's failure domain and installing Tailscale directly on the host for permanent out-of-band access.

item.title: The VM That Wouldn't Start
item.description: A Proxmox kernel update, a stopped OPNsense VM, a stale ISO reference, and why physical console access is worth more than you think.

item.title: Monitoring Every Node
item.description: Installing Glances on four Proxmox nodes, wiring its REST API into the Homepage dashboard, and the pip dependency conflict that made it more interesting than expected.

item.title: Chasing Ghosts, Finding Watts
item.description: A long afternoon chasing phantom reboots on a Proxmox node — ruling out everything, finding nothing definitive, and accidentally building out full UPS monitoring along the way.

item.title: A Tour of the Homelab
item.description: A visual walkthrough of a four-node Proxmox homelab — network architecture, infrastructure services, monitoring, and backups.

item.title: Network Segmentation — VLANs in the Homelab
item.description: Implementing VLAN segmentation with OPNsense and a managed switch — the concept, the configuration, and why network isolation matters.

item.title: Upgrading a Node the Right Way
item.description: Swapping out a Proxmox cluster node for faster hardware — live VM migration, hardware replacement, and what the process teaches about infrastructure resilience.

item.title: Studying With Something at Stake
item.description: Focused Network+ study with a real deadline — a conversation with a networking manager at my employer, and what two weeks of preparation actually looks like.

item.title: A Door Opens
item.description: An email from my company's Network Engineering Manager — what it means, how I responded, and what the next two weeks look like.

item.title: Planka, Persistence, and Layered Proxies
item.description: Two days troubleshooting Planka's websocket issue through a reverse proxy — what broke, what fixed it, and what the process taught me about layered NGINX configs.

item.title: Real Backups, Finally
item.description: Deploying Proxmox Backup Server on a homelab node — datastores, deduplication, retention policies, and why backups matter before you need them.

item.title: 25 Certifications and a Full-Time Job
item.description: A look at six months of self-directed learning — 25+ credentials across infrastructure, development, design, and project management, built around a full-time job and a family.

item.title: Building a Homelab Dashboard
item.description: Setting up Homepage dashboard with live Proxmox stats, wildcard SSL, and the YAML config workflow that comes with it.

item.description: A full restyle of michaelrooney.dev — new typography, warm dark theme, and a public journal section.

item.description: A summary of my experiences building and maintaining a home lab infrastructure for learning and experimentation.

item.description: Mapping all eight CI/CD pipeline phases to actual homelab infrastructure for a coursework assignment.

item.description: A Proxmox firewall cleanup broke OPNsense. What happened, how I fixed it, and what I learned.
